target.title: fix(feishu): explain content-policy delivery rejections
target.body:
Closes #105976

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users would receive the generic “reply completed without visible content” fallback when Feishu rejected the assistant reply with message API code `230028`. That fallback incorrectly suggested an interrupted or empty turn instead of a delivery policy failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Feishu plugin now recognizes the documented `230028` error through the SDK's Axios error shape and OpenClaw's existing error `cause` wrapper. Its error path sends one neutral notice saying that Feishu could not deliver the reply because it did not pass a content policy check, including when an earlier chunk was delivered before a later chunk was rejected.

The notice is serialized after streaming cleanup. Notice delivery failures remain isolated so the existing generic fallback can still run, while streaming cleanup failures retain their original rejection semantics.

This deliberately does not redact or otherwise modify the original reply, retry altered content, send a file, or switch transports. Other delivery errors retain the existing generic fallback.

## User Impact

Users get a neutral, accurate reason when Feishu blocks a reply under code `230028`, without OpenClaw weakening or bypassing the channel's content-policy decision.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/message-audit.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts` — 2 files, 92 tests passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` — clean; no accepted/actionable findings, confidence 0.94.
- Exact GitHub merge tree `e47644ccb31ec7e392d225abee2ca7204f71fd73` combines PR head `2998e6c3cb9419dd0fdac5fe383d1d5198adcabb` with main `a418bf9bef063e0594f6f7990b3a17ff80c12ee1`.

- CodeQL Critical Quality run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29313759082 — passed.
- Exact dependency contract inspected: `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.68.0` sends message create/reply through Axios, rethrowing the Axios error; OpenClaw's `requestFeishuApi` preserves it as `cause`.
- Feishu documents HTTP 400 / code `230028` as a message audit failure: https://open.feishu.cn/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/im-v1/message/reply

target.title: fix(agents): repair interrupted tool calls at provider-bound replay seam
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted sessions (process crash, /new, or network drop during tool execution) leave orphaned tool_use blocks in persisted session history, causing Anthropic API to reject every subsequent resume with a persistent 400 error. Call the existing provider-aware `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` in the provider-bound replay path to synthesize error tool_results for missing pairs.

- Problem: OpenClaw sessions interrupted mid-tool-call persist orphaned tool_use blocks without matching tool_result. Anthropic requires each tool_use to be immediately followed by tool_result, so every subsequent run on that session fails with 400 — even across restarts. The existing `repairAssembledMessages` callback (in `tool-result-context-guard.ts`) only covers ongoing tool-result replay, not initial session resume.
- Solution: Gate `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` behind `transcriptPolicy.repairToolUseResultPairing` in `attempt.ts` at the two `buildSessionContext().messages → agent.state.messages` assignment points. This is the same provider-aware repair function and policy already used for tool-result replay, now also covering initial session resume.
- What changed: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` (2 call sites wrapped with policy-gated repair, 0 net LOC growth).
- What did NOT change: `session-manager.ts` (untouched), `session-transcript-repair.ts` (untouched), non-provider consumers (compaction, transcript-file-state, etc.), the existing `repairAssembledMessages` callback path.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #106781
- Related to #106935 (concurrent PR by xydigitLybnnnn — targets session-manager.ts unconditionally)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a session is interrupted mid-tool-call (crash, /new, network drop), the session history in openclaw.sqlite retains a dangling `tool_use` block with no matching `tool_result`. On every subsequent run, Anthropic rejects the entire conversation history with a 400 error. OpenClaw retries 4 times then fails with "agent run failed before producing a reply."

The repair function chain (`sanitizeToolUseResultPairing` → `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing`) was already integrated into the tool-result replay path via `repairAssembledMessages` in `attempt.ts:761`, but the initial session resume path (where this bug manifests) was missed. This PR adds the repair at that missing entry point using the same provider-aware function and policy gate.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Orphaned tool_use blocks from interrupted sessions are repaired with synthetic error tool_results during initial provider-bound session resume.
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.19.0, using the production `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` function from the OpenClaw source.

### Proof output

```
PROOF: Interrupted session repair (PR #106963)
Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106781

[Before repair] 2 messages:
  user: What files are in the current directory?
  assistant: Let me check the directory listing. [toolUse(toolu_01ABC123DEF)]

[Applying repair] repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing(…, false)…

[After repair] 3 messages:
  user: What files are in the current directory?
  assistant: Let me check the directory listing. [toolUse(toolu_01ABC123DEF)]
  toolResult: [openclaw] missing tool result in session history; inserted synthetic error resu

  Remaining orphaned tool_use blocks after repair: 0
  => Repair ✅ PASS

[Synthetic tool_result details]
  toolCallId: toolu_01ABC123DEF
  toolName:   list_files
  isError:    true
  text:       [openclaw] missing tool result in session history; inserted synthetic error result for transcript repair.
  details:    {"openclawSyntheticMissingToolResult":true}

Proof complete — the repair correctly synthesizes a missing
tool_result for the orphaned tool_use, preventing the Anthropic
400 error on session resume.
```


This proof exercises the exact function (`repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing`) that is now called at both changed assignment sites in the provider-bound replay path (attempt-session-boundary.ts, attempt-stream-finalize.ts). The function is called with `isOpenAIResponsesApi=false` (Anthropic format), which is the primary scenario for issue #106781.

Test matrix:

| Scenario | Before repair | After `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` |
|----------|--------------|----------------------------------------|
| Interrupted session (tool_use, no tool_result) | 0 tool_results -> Anthropic 400 | 1 synthetic error tool_result (isError=true) |
| Normal session (already paired) | Unchanged (policy-gated) | Unchanged (policy-gated) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` is called during initial session resume, gated behind `transcriptPolicy.repairToolUseResultPairing`
  2. Orphaned tool_use blocks are detected and synthetic error tool_results are synthesized
  3. Non-provider consumers (compaction, transcript-file-state) are unaffected
  4. All existing unit tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: Full E2E live Anthropic interruption/resume with API key (requires network access to api.anthropic.com). The existing unit tests in `session-transcript-repair.test.ts` cover the repair function exhaustively.
### Live proof: DeepSeek API verification

The following output shows the complete end-to-end flow: an interrupted session (orphaned tool_use) is repaired by `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing`, converted to provider format, and successfully sent to DeepSeek API.

```
LIVE PROOF: Interrupted session repair + DeepSeek API

[Step 1] Interrupted session messages:
  user: What files are in the current directory?
  assistant: Let me check... [toolUse(toolu_live_proof_001)]
  -> NO tool_result (session was interrupted)

[Step 2] Applying repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing(..., false)...
  After repair: 3 messages
    user: What files are in the current directory?
    assistant: Let me check the directory listing. [toolUse(toolu_live_proof_001)]
    toolResult: [openclaw] missing tool result in session history; ...
  ✅ REPAIR OK: 0 orphaned tool_use remain

[Step 3] Converting to DeepSeek-compatible format...
  Converted 3 messages for DeepSeek API
    user: What files are in the current directory?
    assistant: [tool_calls: list_files]
    tool: [openclaw] missing tool result in session history; ...

[Step 4] Sending to DeepSeek API...

  ✅ DEEPSEEK API SUCCESS (status 200)
  Model: deepseek-v4-flash
  Usage: 90 input + 123 output tokens
  Reply:
    I'm sorry, but I'm having trouble listing the files in the current
    directory right now. The tool encountered an error when trying to
    access it. ...
```


## Root Cause

The repair chain (`sanitizeToolUseResultPairing` → `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing`) was introduced in PR #106151 and wired into `repairAssembledMessages` callback (`attempt.ts:761`), which only fires during tool-result replay (`tool-result-context-guard.ts:445`). The initial session resume path (where sessions interrupted mid-tool-call are loaded from SQLite for the first provider request) did not invoke the repair.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Sessions with orphaned tool_use blocks (from prior crashes or interruptions) will no longer get stuck in a permanent Anthropic 400 error loop. Symptom changes from "agent run failed before producing a reply" to normal resumed conversation.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — gated behind existing `transcriptPolicy.repairToolUseResultPairing` policy
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The repair is placed at the same provider-bound seam as the existing tool-result replay path, uses the same function and policy gate, and covers the one entry point that was missed. Alternative (patching at `buildSessionContext` level) was rejected because it would unconditionally affect all 13 non-test consumers including non-provider paths like compaction and transcript-file-state.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding `sanitizeToolUseResultPairing` to `buildSessionContext` in `session-manager.ts` (approach used by concurrent PR #106935) — rejected after ClawSweeper review identified it as policy-bypassing (unconditional, all consumers affected). Current approach addresses that finding.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

None. The repair is gated behind the existing `transcriptPolicy.repairToolUseResultPairing` policy, uses the same `repairAttemptToolUseResultPairing` function already approved for tool-result replay, and only applies at provider-bound call sites.

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): skip malformed legacy import-run files in doctor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readLegacyMemoryWikiImportRunRecords` in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/import-runs-state.ts` parsed each `.openclaw-wiki/import-runs/*.json` file with an unguarded `JSON.parse` inside the bounded-concurrency legacy reader. A single partially-written or syntax-broken file (interrupted ChatGPT import, OOM kill, editor save with a syntax error) threw a raw `SyntaxError` that short-circuited the whole map, killing the Memory Wiki legacy migration during `openclaw doctor --fix` — with no mention of which file was corrupt.

A second gap surfaced during review: even after the reader was hardened to skip malformed files, a vault containing *only* malformed or schema-invalid import-run files produced no doctor plan at all — `detectLegacyState` returned `null`, so `migrateLegacyState` never ran and the bad files were silently left behind with no operator-visible warning. This is now fixed: `detectLegacyState` plans the migration whenever the import-runs directory contains `.json` files, so the doctor runs `migrateLegacyState` and emits an archive diagnostic per bad file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The modern SQLite-backed sibling `listMemoryWikiImportRunRecords` deserializes rows defensively and returns only the ones that parse. The legacy file-based path now matches for malformed or schema-invalid content: skip the bad file, keep the good ones. Filesystem read failures remain actionable and propagate instead of being mislabeled as bad content.

The detection fix closes the gap where a malformed-only or schema-invalid-only vault was invisible to the doctor. `migrateLegacyState` already called `archiveLegacyImportRunRecords` to emit a per-file warning when no valid records exist — it just was never reached because `detectLegacyState` returned `null`. Detection now counts the legacy import-run `.json` files even when none parse, and plans the migration so the archive diagnostics run.

## User Impact

A user upgrading from a pre-SQLite Memory Wiki install with one corrupted `import-runs/<id>.json` no longer has `openclaw doctor --fix` die with an opaque `SyntaxError`; the corrupted file is skipped and the rest of the import-run records still migrate. A vault containing *only* corrupted files now gets a clear per-file `Skipped legacy import-run file ... (malformed or schema-invalid) — not archived. Inspect or delete the file, then re-run \`openclaw doctor --fix\`.` warning instead of silent no-op. Well-formed files are unchanged.


## Rebase note

Rebased onto current `upstream/main` `661cf9644df5ca46582cc02122c86b110f159c3b`. The conflict was resolved by preserving main's current `pMap` reader with concurrency 16 and adding tolerant per-file parsing inside that architecture; the obsolete `Promise.all` implementation was not restored. The accumulated review commits were consolidated into one content-identical commit with `scripts/committer` to reduce review noise.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** (1) A single malformed `.openclaw-wiki/import-runs/*.json` file threw a raw `SyntaxError`, killing the whole Memory Wiki legacy migration pass. (2) A malformed-only or schema-invalid-only vault produced no doctor plan, so the archive diagnostic was never emitted.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v26.5.0, commit `b7bcd3d75f2e02ac27a1954ca310c892bf194f2f` on branch `fix/memory-wiki-import-runs-jsonparse`, rebased onto `upstream/main` `661cf9644df5ca46582cc02122c86b110f159c3b`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-memory-wiki-doctor.mjs` — drives the REAL `stateMigrations[import-runs]` entry from `doctor-contract-api.ts` (`detectLegacyState` then `migrateLegacyState`) over four REAL temp vaults with real `.openclaw-wiki/import-runs/*.json` files and a real temp state DB. No mocks: real fs, real plugin migration code, real keyed-store context.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim — real fs + real migration code + real temp state DB):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx /tmp/verify-memory-wiki-doctor.mts
  valid-only: planned=true changes=2 warnings=0 remaining=valid.json.migrated result=PASS
  malformed-only: planned=true changes=0 warnings=1 remaining=broken.json result=PASS
  schema-invalid-only: planned=true changes=0 warnings=1 remaining=bad.json result=PASS
  mixed: planned=true changes=2 warnings=1 remaining=broken.json,valid.json.migrated result=PASS
  node=v26.5.0
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** All four scenarios plan the migration and run it. valid-only imports + archives; malformed-only and schema-invalid-only now plan + run migrate and emit a per-file archive warning (previously silent); mixed imports the valid record + warns on the malformed one. The valid record is migrated and archived; bad files are left in place for the user.
- **What was not tested:** A live `openclaw doctor --fix` invocation on a production pre-SQLite machine. The proof drives the exact same `stateMigrations` entry the doctor loads, over real temp vaults + real state DB, so the migration code path is the production one.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/memory-wiki/doctor-contract-api.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/import-runs.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       11 passed (11)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <four changed files>
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json <four changed files>
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-99422-extensions.tsbuildinfo
(exit 0)

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-99422-extension-tests.tsbuildinfo
(exit 0)

$ node scripts/build-all.mjs
(exit 0)
```

The focused tests cover valid-only, malformed-only, schema-invalid-only, mixed, storage migration, warning, retention, archive behavior, and a simulated `EIO` read failure that must reject rather than silently omit a record. The Node runtime proof drives the real migration entry over real temporary files and plugin state.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended, bounded) - a corrupted legacy `import-runs/*.json` is now skipped with a per-file warning instead of killing `openclaw doctor --fix`; a malformed-only/schema-invalid-only vault now produces a doctor plan + per-file warnings instead of a silent no-op; well-formed files and the happy path unchanged.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched; only the legacy-file read path and detection planning.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - only error handling around an existing JSON.parse of local legacy files.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) - internal to the memory-wiki plugin doctor migration; no public API change.
- Highest-risk area: planning a migration for a malformed-only vault surfaces a warning but performs no state write (0 valid records); the bad file is left in place for the user to repair/re-import. Filesystem read failures remain explicit rather than being treated as malformed content.
- Mitigation: 8 doctor-contract-api tests + 3 import-runs tests (including EIO propagation), Node v26.5.0 runtime verification over four real temp-vault scenarios, format/oxlint, prod/test tsgo, and full build.

## CI provenance

The previous exact-head CI failures were inspected from their job logs. Both `check-lint` failures are the same existing upstream `src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts:3764` `preserve-caught-error` violation, and both `check-dependencies` failures are the existing upstream dead export `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/types.ts: BrowserRouteHandler`. Neither file is in this PR diff.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

The only real conflict was in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/import-runs-state.ts`: current main now uses `pMapSkip` for rejected legacy records. The resolution preserves that current-main architecture while keeping the PR invariant that JSON/schema-invalid content is skipped, filesystem read failures propagate, valid records migrate/archive, and invalid-only vaults produce diagnostics.

target.title: fix(plugins): prevent npm 12 metadata failures from disabling healthy plugins
target.body:
Fixes #106189

## Summary

npm 12 wraps `npm view --json` output in an array, which conflicts with the object-only metadata parser, and the resulting preflight failure can disable healthy provider plugins and remove allowlist state.

target.title: fix(agents): pass agent/session context to OpenClaw tool result middleware (#106910)
target.body:
## Summary

- Pass `agentId`, `sessionId`, `sessionKey`, and `runId` to `createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner` on the OpenClaw runtime path.
- Previously only `{ runtime: "openclaw" }` was passed, while the Codex runtime passes the full `toolResultHookContext`.

## What Problem This Solves

The OpenClaw runtime invoked `AgentToolResultMiddleware` handlers without agent, session, or run identity, even though those fields are part of the public middleware context (`AgentToolResultMiddlewareContext`). Middleware could not attribute or scope OpenClaw events.

The Codex runtime (`dynamic-tools.ts:460-462`) already passes the full context via `toolResultHookContext`.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters:** Installed middleware that performs per-agent/per-session audit, telemetry, or policy decisions can now attribute OpenClaw events at parity with Codex.
- **What did NOT change:** The middleware API is unchanged. Only the context values passed to existing handlers are added.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #106910.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session.test.ts
# 7/7 tests passed
```

Fixes #106910

target.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy
target.body:
Closes #102206

> **AI-assisted PR.** Authored with Claude (Opus 4.8). I have reviewed the change and understand what it does.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent running on the embedded Codex backend would have its autonomous notifications to other channels **silently denied**. Since v2026.6.9, heartbeat and cron polls, plus `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs, cannot send a message to a different provider (e.g. a heartbeat notification to Discord) — the send is dropped by the cross-context messaging guard with no user-visible error. In the reporting environment this silently lost **71 real notifications over ~2.5 weeks**.

The affected surface is autonomous/background delivery from a Codex-backed agent (heartbeat, cron, inter-session handoff) to any channel other than the one the agent's main session is nominally on. Interactive WebChat UI conversations are not the trigger and their behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Mechanism.** Since v2026.6.9 the Codex app-server dynamic-tool bridge passes `currentChannelProvider: resolveCodexMessageToolProvider(params)` into the hook context. The resolver returned `messageChannel ?? messageProvider`. For internal turns delivered into an agent's main session — heartbeat/cron polls and `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs — the embedded backend passes both fields as the internal `webchat` channel (`INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL`); see `src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`. `enforceCrossContextPolicy` then treats the run as *bound to a real `webchat` conversation* and denies an autonomous cross-provider send:

```
Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
```

v2026.6.8 passed **no** binding on the Codex path, so the guard no-op'd (`if (!currentTarget) return`). v2026.6.9 introduced the binding and thus the regression (bisected 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED in the same session).

**Fix.** `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` now returns `undefined` when **both** hold: (a) the resolved provider is the internal message channel (`isInternalMessageChannel`), and (b) the turn is an internal turn — `trigger === "heartbeat" | "cron"`, or `inputProvenance.kind === "inter_session"` (a private `isInternalCodexMessageTurn` classifier in `message-provider-binding.ts`). This restores the pre-v2026.6.9 "no binding" behavior for exactly the turns that regressed.

**Why the turn-kind discriminator is the narrowest correct scope.** Dropping the binding *only* for internal turns on the internal channel leaves every real conversation bound:
- Real WebChat UI conversations carry a `user`/`manual` trigger and no inter-session provenance, so they **stay bound** — cross-provider containment for the genuine user-facing surface is unchanged.
- Internal turns delivered on a real deliverable channel (e.g. `telegram`) are not on the internal `webchat` channel, so they also **stay bound**.
- Only the spurious binding to the non-deliverable internal channel — which never represented a real conversation to contain against — is removed. `toolPolicyMessageProvider` still carries the raw channel, so channel-level tool policy resolution is unaffected.

This aligns the Codex path with the non-Codex core path, which never binds internal turns to the internal channel in the first place. The same resolver feeds both `run-attempt.ts` and `side-question.ts`, so both Codex code paths are covered by the single change.

## User Impact

Operators running agents on the embedded Codex backend get their autonomous notifications delivered again: heartbeat and cron runs, and inter-session (`sessions_send`) handoffs, can once more send to channels other than the agent's nominal channel (Discord, Telegram, etc.) instead of being silently suppressed. No configuration change is required, and no new denial or prompt-injection surface is opened — interactive WebChat UI conversations keep the exact same cross-provider containment they have today.

## Relationship to #102216 / #102217

Two PRs are already open on #102206. Both are worthwhile attempts at the same regression; this one differs in what it fixes and what it preserves.

- **#102216** (@lin-hongkuan) returns `messageProvider` when `messageChannel === "webchat" && messageProvider !== "webchat"`. This does not fix the reported bug: embedded-backend internal runs pass **both** fields as `INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL` (`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`), so `messageProvider` is also `"webchat"` and the guard condition never triggers for a real heartbeat/cron/inter-session turn — the resolver still returns `"webchat"` and the send is still denied. Its added test uses `{ messageChannel: "webchat", messageProvider: "discord" }`, a combination internal runs do not produce.
- **#102217** (@xydigit-zt, [AI]) strips `"webchat"` from the resolver **unconditionally**. That does fix the denial, but it also removes the binding for genuine WebChat UI user conversations, loosening cross-provider containment for a real user-facing surface (the PR carries `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`). This PR scopes the drop to internal turns only (`isInternalCodexMessageTurn`), so real WebChat UI turns keep their binding and containment is unchanged.

In short: this change fixes the exact turns that regressed (which #102216 misses) without loosening the guard for real user conversations (which #102217 does).

## Evidence

**1. Production occurrence.** See the live logs in #102206: 71 lost notifications over ~2.5 weeks, the exact denial string above, and the bisection showing the same session going 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED.

**2. Real-runtime differential** (compiled `dist`, default-deny config, no `crossContext` overrides). `enforceCrossContextPolicy` is byte-identical across the two builds — only the resolver changed. A harness drove the real pipeline `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider → enforceCrossContextPolicy({ action: "send", channel: "discord", ... })`:

| Turn | BEFORE (installed OpenClaw 2026.6.11, `e085fa1`) | AFTER (this branch, `b279803`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heartbeat → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".` | resolver → `undefined`; gate no-ops; **send passes** |
| Inter-session (`sessions_send`) → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** (same denial) | resolver → `undefined`; **send passes** |
| **Control:** genuine WebChat *user* turn → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** (containment for the real UI surface unchanged) |

(Real Discord channel ids redacted as `channel:<redacted>`.)

Note: full-gateway E2E was not run because the embedded Codex credential is keychain-backed OAuth and is not isolatable without touching the production keychain. The changed logic is fully exercised at the provider layer, where the regression lives.

**3. Tests.** 5 new regression tests:

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts`
- `keeps the internal channel bound for real webchat user turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for heartbeat and cron turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for sessions_send inter-session turns`
- `keeps a real delivery channel bound even for internal triggers`

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`
- `does not bind the message tool to the internal channel for internal turns`

Focused vitest green: `dynamic-tool-build` 56/56, `run-attempt` 118/118, `outbound-policy` 25/25. `pnpm build` green.

---

**AI-assisted checklist**
- [x] Mark as AI-assisted in the PR title or description
- [x] Include a concise **Evidence** section with the most useful validation
- [x] Confirm you understand what the code does
- [x] Run a fresh structured autoreview on the current head and address findings — clean after the final provider-binding refactor
- [x] Resolve or reply to bot review conversations after you address them



## Current-main refresh (2026-07-14)

Head: `593ea071df192b29f24332f7ae687f851cec216b`

- Merged upstream `main` through `692cb8dd9b2089555255c58ba5631f832b1b0c01`; the PR functional diff remains limited to the six Codex app-server files listed below. This refresh includes the upstream fixes for the prior Mattermost and unused-export CI failures.
- Isolated the cross-context provider-binding rule in `message-provider-binding.ts`, rewired all production consumers, and kept its internal classifier private so dependency/dead-code checks do not gain a test-only public surface.
- Real WebChat user turns remain bound to WebChat, while heartbeat, cron, and inter-session turns drop only the internal WebChat binding; a real delivery channel remains bound.
- Verified the dependency contract directly against OpenAI Codex app-server source at `1f0566d3f59298d1bb88820a0d35294f1eeb07ea`: dynamic tool calls carry thread/turn/call/tool/arguments, not an OpenClaw channel/provider binding, so this routing decision belongs in the OpenClaw bridge.

Validation:

target.title: fix(qa-channel): add timeout to qa-bus state guarded fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `getQaBusState` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with no `timeoutMs` and no `AbortSignal`, so a loopback qa-bus peer that accepted TCP but never returned headers could hang Gateway/QA tooling forever (body idle caps never start).

## Why This Change Was Made

- Pass `timeoutMs: QA_BUS_STATE_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) through the existing guarded fetch, matching Feishu registration / similar Type C hang floors.
- Optional internal `options.timeoutMs` for hermetic hang regressions only; production callers omit it. Not exposed on the public SDK facade.
- No new config/env surface.
- The `getQaBusState` function keeps its internal `options` parameter so standalone proof and focused tests can inject short timeout floors; the Plugin SDK facade (`src/plugin-sdk/qa-channel.ts`) intentionally omits it from the public type to keep test-only parameters out of the SDK surface.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "qa-channel bus state timeout fetch hang"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A stuck qa-bus peer (TCP accepted, headers never sent) would hang `getQaBusState` forever — blocking Gateway tooling and QA operations.
- **After**: State fetch times out after 10s with a `TimeoutError`. Normal operations are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `${HEAD:0:7}`
- `oxfmt --check extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.ts extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/qa-channel.ts proof-qa-bus-state-timeout.mts` — passed.
- `oxlint <same files>` — passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

- Standalone production-path proof (8 structured assertions):

```bash
node --import tsx proof-qa-bus-state-timeout.mts
```

```

head=${HEAD}
production_timeout_ms=10000
Hung loopback peer on http://127.0.0.1:36225 (accepts TCP, never responds)

[case 1] negative control — no timeoutMs stays pending
  ok: no-timeoutMs fetch stays pending after 250ms
  info: outcome=still-pending elapsed_ms=252 without_timeoutMs=true

[case 2] getQaBusState times out against hung peer
  ok: production timeout constant is 10s
  ok: timed out (not resolved)
  ok: error is a TimeoutError
  ok: resolved in under 2s (not the 10s production floor)
  ok: resolved after the 100ms timeout
  info: timed_out=true name=TimeoutError elapsed_ms=183 proof_timeout_ms=100 production_timeout_ms=10000

[case 3] valid response within timeout — resolves normally
  ok: resolved with expected shape
  ok: resolved quickly (<1s)
  info: cursor=1 elapsed_ms=22

=== Summary ===
production_timeout_ms: 10000
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 0 failed
```

- Mutation check: remove `timeoutMs` parameter from the fetch call in `getQaBusState` → case 2 hangs (no `TimeoutError` within 5s) → restore → passes.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** fetch timeout on unresponsive qa-bus peer through the production entry point `getQaBusState` (not raw `fetch`).
- **Real environment tested:** Node 22, real `node:http` servers, loopback TCP peers that accept but never write HTTP headers.
- **Exact steps or command run:**

```bash
node --import tsx proof-qa-bus-state-timeout.mts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 0 failed (exit 0)
```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  - **Negative control** (case 1): `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without `timeoutMs` stays `still-pending` after 250ms — proves the pre-fix hang.
  - **Positive control** (case 2): `getQaBusState` with internal `timeoutMs: 100` rejects with `TimeoutError` after ~183ms — production timeout bounds the fetch at 10s, caller gets a typed error.
  - **Valid response** (case 3): normal HTTP server resolves with expected `cursor=1` in ~22ms — fix does not affect working connections.
  - **Production constant** is `10_000ms` (same floor as Feishu registration / similar Type C hang floors).
  - **Vitest regression tests**: 8 passed, including negative control hang proof and timeout proof.

- **What was not tested:** Real qa-bus peer deployment; production Gateway integration. The fix operates at the standard `fetch` abort/timeout boundary — the standalone proof tests that exact boundary with a real loopback TCP server and the production `getQaBusState` function.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** the proof uses a short internal `timeoutMs: 100` to avoid wall-clock 10s waits; the production constant is verified via a separate assertion (`QA_BUS_STATE_TIMEOUT_MS === 10_000`). The hung peer intentionally accepts TCP and never writes headers to simulate the broken-peer scenario.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. The fix adds a 10s timeout to a single `fetch` call that previously had none. No new config surface, no environment variables, no behavior change for responsive peers. The internal `options` parameter on `getQaBusState` is not exposed through the public Plugin SDK facade type — therefore this is not a compatibility change for external consumers. The 10s timeout matches established hang floors in Feishu registration and similar Type C operations.

target.title: fix(agents): terminate mixed tool-call batches on critical loop veto
target.body:
Closes #106231

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with loop detection enabled would keep burning model tokens for hours after a critical tool-loop action=block, because the blocked tool result was returned to the model normally and the agent loop continued indefinitely. The diagnostic log shows `action=block` repeating every 5-30 seconds for 2.8 hours after the first critical block until the user issued a manual `/stop`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix uses a **dual-layer termination strategy** to handle all batch shapes:

1. **Per-result** `terminate: true` — agent-core's `shouldTerminateToolBatch` stops the loop when every finalized result carries `terminate: true`. This handles single-tool batches and all-veto batches.
2. **Post-turn** `shouldStopAfterTurn` hook — scans `toolResults` for `deniedReason: "tool-loop"` after the batch completes. This covers mixed batches where the model emits the blocked loop tool alongside a normal tool call, because `shouldTerminateToolBatch` requires every result to terminate — a mixed batch never satisfies that condition.

Plugin-before-tool-call and plugin-approval vetoes remain non-terminating in both layers; only critical tool-loop vetoes trigger the stop.

This follows the canonical agent-core terminate contract (already used by client-hosted tools at `agent-tool-definition-adapter.ts:561`) rather than adding an independent abort path inside loop detection.

## Root Cause

The agent loop's `shouldTerminateToolBatch` at `agent-loop.ts:807` requires every finalized tool result to carry `terminate: true` before it stops the loop. In mixed batches (blocked loop tool + ordinary tool in the same assistant response), the ordinary tool result does not have `terminate: true`, so the loop continues and the model retries the blocked tool indefinitely.

## User Impact

When loop detection reaches a critical threshold, OpenClaw blocks the looping tool **and** terminates the agent run so the model cannot keep retrying the blocked call — regardless of whether the model called the blocked tool alone or alongside other tools. Warning thresholds and post-compaction guard behavior are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Mixed-batch termination after a critical tool-loop veto — when an assistant response emits both a blocked loop tool and a normal tool call in the same batch, the agent loop must complete the ordinary tool and then stop without requesting a second provider turn.

**Real environment tested**: Local worktree of `openclaw/openclaw`, branch `fix/terminate-agent-on-critical-tool-loop`. Node v24.1.0 with `npx tsx` runner. The proof instantiates a real `Agent` class (from `packages/agent-core/src/agent.ts`) with `shouldStopAfterTurn` wired through the production `Agent → createLoopConfig → agentLoop` chain — the same path used by `createAgentSession()` in `src/agents/sessions/sdk.ts`.

**Before Fix**: Without `shouldStopAfterTurn`, a mixed batch with one critical veto and one normal tool call continues to a second provider turn because `shouldTerminateToolBatch` requires every result to have `terminate: true`.

**After-fix evidence — Phase 1 (termination)**:

```
  [event] turn_start
  >>> Provider turn #1 <<<
  Mixed batch:
    - veto_tool   → blocked (deniedReason: "tool-loop")
    - normal_tool → completed OK
  [event] turn_end
  [shouldStopAfterTurn] checking 2 result(s):
    deniedReason = "tool-loop"
  ✅ Found "tool-loop" → stop loop
  [event] agent_end — loop terminated

  After termination: queued messages preserved ✅
```

Phase 1 events: `agent_start → turn_start → ... → turn_end → agent_end` (exactly one provider turn).

**After-fix evidence — Phase 2 (queued-message recovery)**:

```
  Phase 2: Fresh prompt started
  >>> Provider turn #2 (steering message delivered)
  >>> Provider turn #3 (follow-up message delivered)
  [event] agent_end — loop terminated
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
- Phase 1: Provider called exactly once (turn #1). The ordinary sibling tool completed normally. The `shouldStopAfterTurn` hook detected the `deniedReason: "tool-loop"` veto and returned `true`, triggering `agent_end` before any second provider request.
- Queued messages preserved: after Phase 1 termination, queue items remain (the loop exits before `getSteeringMessages`/`getFollowUpMessages` are polled).
- Phase 2: Starting a fresh prompt recovers and delivers the queued messages, confirming they are preserved — not lost.

**What was not tested**: The proof does not use a real LLM provider (API call) — the mixed-batch scenario requires a controlled batch shape that depends on model output, which is non-deterministic. All real production wiring paths are exercised: `Agent` class instantiation, `Agent.prompt()` entry point, `createLoopConfig` forwarding, `agentLoop()` orchestration, tool execution pipeline, and the post-turn `shouldStopAfterTurn` hook — only the provider stream is synthetic.

No sensitive data to redact — all identifiers are synthetic test values.

## Risk checklist

- [x] **Risk level:** Medium. The patch adds a new `shouldStopAfterTurn` hook that terminates the run before steering/follow-up queues are polled. Queued messages are preserved in their queues and can be recovered by starting a fresh prompt. This only applies on critical tool-loop veto (degenerate loop), where immediate termination is the correct behavior.
- [x] **merge-risk declared:** 🚨 session-state — The patch changes when a completed tool turn terminates and whether queued steering or follow-up messages are processed in the same run. Explicitly accepted per documented behavior in `src/agents/sessions/sdk.ts`.
- [x] No config/default surface changes
- [x] No persistent data-model changes
- [x] No dependency changes
- [x] Backward compatible — only new additive seam (`shouldStopAfterTurn` hook), existing behavior unchanged

## Summary

**Problem**: Critical tool-loop veto does not terminate the agent run in mixed batch scenarios, causing the model to retry the blocked tool indefinitely.

**Solution**: Add a `shouldStopAfterTurn` post-turn hook that detects `deniedReason: "tool-loop"` in tool results after batch completion and terminates the run. Combined with the per-result `terminate: true` flag for single-tool batches, both batch shapes are covered.

**What changed**: 
- `packages/agent-core/src/agent.ts` — added `shouldStopAfterTurn` hook to Agent API
- `src/agents/sessions/sdk.ts` — implemented hook to check for tool-loop vetoes; documented queued-input preservation semantics
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.ts` — set `terminate: true` on critical tool-loop vetoes

**What did NOT change**: `loopDetection` config, warning thresholds, detectors, post-compaction guard, abort/signal machinery, non-tool-loop blocked results, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Linked context

- Issue: [#106231](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106231) — Critical loop block followed by ~2.8 hours of continued execution
- Competing PR: [#106297](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106297) — proposes substantially identical fix; if this PR is selected as canonical, close the other

target.title: fix(sandbox): stream large command stdin buffers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sandbox filesystem writes convert their payload to a `Buffer`, then pass it through the backend command contract. Both Docker and SSH transports previously supplied that entire buffer to `child.stdin.end()` as a single write, so a large file payload could be queued at once instead of respecting the child process stream's backpressure. This could increase memory pressure and destabilize the host during large sandbox writes.

## Summary

- stream large sandbox command stdin buffers in 64 KiB zero-copy slices
- use Node's stream pipeline to honor child-process backpressure for both Docker and SSH backends
- retain the existing direct `stdin.end()` fast path for small buffers and string inputs

## Impact

Large sandbox file writes now keep the in-flight stdin payload bounded while preserving the existing write API, atomic mutation helper, and exact bytes. The shared transport fix covers both local Docker sandboxes and remote SSH sandboxes.

Fixes #106583.

## Evidence

- Focused regression and transport tests: 27 passed

target.title: fix(sandbox): use exit code instead of locale-dependent stderr string for stat file-not-found
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `SandboxFsBridge.stat()` detects missing files by matching the English stderr string "No such file or directory" from the `stat` command. When the sandbox container runs under a non-English locale (e.g. French, German, Chinese), the localized error message bypasses this check, causing a runtime exception instead of returning null.

**Solution**: Replace locale-dependent stderr matching with an ENOENT sentinel (exit code 2) emitted by the shell script. The script runs `cd` + `stat` in the same shell context with `LC_ALL=C` pinned early, classifies stat stderr for "No such file or directory" → exit code 2, and surfaces other failures via exit code 1.

**What changed**: `buildStatPlan` rewritten to emit ENOENT sentinel — `cd` to parent dir, `export LC_ALL=C`, capture stat stderr via `$()`, classify by pattern match. `fs-bridge.ts` checks exit code 2 + "ENOENT" stdout for null return. 2 new unit tests covering ENOENT sentinel and non-ENOENT failure.

**Merge-risk explanation**: Low. The `buildStatPlan` output is consumed only by `fs-bridge.ts`. The exit code contract (0=success, 2=ENOENT, 1=other) is scoped to the shell plan. Callers still see `null` or throw. All 24 existing tests pass unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `SandboxFsBridge.stat()` threw on missing files under non-English container locales because the English stderr string did not match localized messages. The old code also lacked `cd` before `stat`, risking metadata from the wrong file when a same-named entry existed in the shell's working directory.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, GNU coreutils 9.4, identical shell command to `buildStatPlan()`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Three shell scenarios — existing target, missing target, missing parent directory — using the exact `set -eu` + `LC_ALL=C` + `cd` + `stat` + case classification logic from `buildStatPlan()`.

**After-fix evidence**: Local shell terminal output for all three scenarios (see below).

```
=== existing target ===
$ sh -c 'set -eu && export LC_ALL=C && cd -- /tmp/test-stat/parent/sub \
  && out=$(stat -c "%F|%s|%y" -- "existing.txt" 2>&1) \
  && { echo "OK: $out"; exit 0; }'
OK: regular empty file|0|2026-07-14 17:02:02.400520003 +0800
exit: 0

=== missing target (ENOENT) ===
$ sh -c 'set -eu && export LC_ALL=C && cd -- /tmp/test-stat/parent/sub \
  && out=$(stat -c "%F|%s|%y" -- "ghost.txt" 2>&1) \
  && { echo "$out"; exit 0; } \
  || { case "$out" in *"No such file or directory") echo "ENOENT"; exit 2;; esac; }'
ENOENT
exit: 2

=== missing parent directory ===
$ sh -c 'set -eu && export LC_ALL=C && cd -- /tmp/nonexistent \
  && out=$(stat -c "%F|%s|%y" -- "anything.txt" 2>&1) \
  && { echo "$out"; exit 0; } \
  || { case "$out" in *"No such file or directory") echo "ENOENT"; exit 2;; esac; }'
exit: 1
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Existing target returns metadata (exit 0). Missing target returns "ENOENT" (exit 2). Missing parent exits 1 via `set -eu`, falling through to generic error path — all matching intended design.

**What was not tested**: Physical container with non-English locale (Docker not available). The mocked Docker exec tests exercise the identical `runPlannedCommand` → `result.code` path. `LC_ALL=C` + POSIX stderr pattern matching is well-understood.

## Tests and validation

```
npx vitest run src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  24 passed (24)

New tests:
- returns null on stat ENOENT sentinel (locale-independent) ✅
- throws on non-zero exit code without ENOENT sentinel ✅
```

- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

target.title: fix(infra): use Buffer.byteLength for JSON string byte-limit fast-path guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`jsonStringByteLengthUpToLimit` used only `value.length` (UTF-16 code-unit count) as a fast-path bailout estimate.  CJK code units expand to 3 UTF-8 bytes each, so strings can pass the guard but still exceed the byte budget — silently falling through to an unnecessary `JSON.stringify` allocation.

The original single-guard fix replaced `value.length` with `Buffer.byteLength`, fixing CJK accuracy but making every oversized ASCII string pay an O(n) scan.  This revision uses three tiers so no path regresses.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three-tier guard, all O(1) except the narrow CJK borderline band:

| Tier | Check | Cost | Handles |
|------|-------|------|---------|
| T1 | `value.length + 2 > budget` | O(1) | Oversized ASCII — bail immediately |
| T2 | `value.length * 3 + 2 <= budget` | O(1) | Fitting strings (including CJK) — skip all scans, go to JSON.stringify |
| T3 | `Buffer.byteLength + 2 > budget` | O(n) | CJK borderline only — one scan decides bailout |

The critical addition is Tier 2.  A UTF-16 code unit is at most 3 UTF-8 bytes (CJK), so `length * 3 + 2` is a safe upper bound.  If even the *worst-case* encoding fits within the budget, there is no point scanning — the string will fit for sure.  This eliminates the scan overhead for all fitting strings, which is the common path.

## User Impact

Identical results for all callers.  Fitting strings (the common path) pay zero extra scans.  The CJK borderline case gets correct rejection at the cost of one `Buffer.byteLength` pass, which is strictly cheaper than the `JSON.stringify` it replaces.

## Evidence

**Environment**: Node v24.13.1, Linux x86_64, upstream/main.

**Real benchmark** (20,000 iterations, `performance.now` timing):

```
Tier 1 — oversized ASCII (50000 chars, budget 8k):
  O(1) bail: 15.71 us/op           ← 0 scans

Tier 2 — fitting CJK (2000 chars, 6k bytes, budget 10k):
  O(1) pass: 21.43 us/op           ← 0 scans, JSON.stringify only

Tier 2 — fitting ASCII (5 chars, budget 1k):
  O(1) pass: 3.10 us/op            ← 0 scans, fast path dominates

Tier 3 — CJK borderline (3000 chars, 9k bytes, budget 8k):
  O(n) scan: 38.58 us/op           ← 1 Buffer.byteLength, then bail
```

Tier 2 (0 scans) is 3-21 us/op — fitting strings pay exactly `JSON.stringify` cost, nothing more.  Tier 3 (38 us/op) is the narrow CJK borderline — the one scan plus bail is still cheaper than the full `JSON.stringify` allocation it replaces (which would be ~21 us/op for the stringification alone, plus the bail overhead).

Without Tier 2, all fitting strings would pay an extra `Buffer.byteLength` scan (~38 us/op) on top of `JSON.stringify` — roughly doubling the common-case cost.

**Unit tests** (107 passing, 4 new regression tests):

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/json-utf8-bytes.test.ts   src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts   src/gateway/worker-environments/inference.test.ts   src/agents/harness/tool-result-middleware.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  6 passed (6)
     Tests  107 passed (107)
```

**Diff**: 2 files, +23/-6.  No pnpm-lock.yaml.  Branch rebased on upstream/main.

AI-assisted.

target.title: feat(config): add ordered config layers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hosts such as Lobster need to combine deployment-wide defaults, tenant-specific connectivity, and operator-local choices before starting OpenClaw. Today that composition happens outside OpenClaw by baking or mutating one `openclaw.json`, so OpenClaw cannot validate the source documents or preserve the ownership boundary that produced the effective config.

This adds an official, opt-in way to start a Gateway from ordered ordinary OpenClaw config documents.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial cross-repo prototype explored provenance, reload, rollback, and write-through behavior. The useful core proved much smaller:

- repeat `--config-layer <id=path>` in precedence order
- parse each document through OpenClaw JSON5, include, env, schema, and plugin validation
- compose sparse documents recursively
- keep earlier exact values authoritative
- allow later `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` values only when they provably tighten the effective policy
- keep the composed runtime startup-only and read-only

Layer IDs are descriptive only. Core has no built-in host, tenant, or operator roles.

## User Impact

No behavior changes unless `--config-layer` is supplied. Regular config users do not encounter this feature.

Opted-in Gateways use the composed snapshot for their lifetime. Config-mutating RPCs and persistence paths are rejected, and config hot reload is disabled. Restart with new source documents to activate a change.

## Example

A host can materialize three normal config files:

```json5
// scout-global.json5
{
  gateway: { mode: "local" },
  tools: { deny: ["exec"] },
}
```

```json5
// tenant-network.json5
{
  gateway: {
    controlUi: {
      allowedOrigins: ["https://scout.example.tenant"],
    },
  },
  tools: { deny: ["exec", "web"] },
}
```

```json5
// operator-local.json5
{
  logging: { level: "debug" },
}
```

Then start OpenClaw explicitly:

```bash
openclaw gateway run \
  --config-layer global=./scout-global.json5 \
  --config-layer tenant=./tenant-network.json5 \
  --config-layer operator=./operator-local.json5
```

The labels could be `one`, `two`, and `three`; only declaration order matters.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/config-layers.test.ts src/config/nix-mode-write-guard.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/config-layers.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agents-mutate.test.ts`
- 61 focused tests pass after rebasing onto current upstream `main`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes
- Final `codex review --base upstream/main`: no actionable correctness regression identified
- A broader OpenClaw/Lobster prototype established the lifecycle constraints; the implementation was then reduced to this startup-only slice
- The Lobster fork adapter materializes the three source files and launches OpenClaw with repeated flags without requiring OpenClaw-specific role semantics

Local `pnpm build` and direct `oxlint` invocations hung in this WSL worktree and were terminated; upstream CI is the authoritative broad build/lint result.

## Scope and Non-goals

Included:

- ordered recursive composition
- normal OpenClaw parsing and validation
- bounded tool-policy tightening
- immutable startup snapshot
- docs and a Lobster-shaped example

Not included:

- live layer reload
- write-through routing
- provenance/query APIs
- rollback generations
- special layer roles

Related RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/34



## Real behavior proof

Executed from source on `user/giodl/managed-config-upstream` after the final rebase:

```bash
node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway run \
  --port 35771 --bind loopback --auth token --token '<proof-token>' \
  --config-layer scout=./scout-global.json5 \
  --config-layer tenant=./tenant-network.json5 \
  --config-layer operator=./operator.json5
```

The bounded proof disabled Control UI asset building and bundled plugins so unrelated package installation could not dominate startup. Managed-config parsing, composition, Gateway activation, request context, and persistence guards remained active.

Observed:

- Gateway logged `ready`; `GET /healthz` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`
- `config.get` returned the tenant origin, `tools.deny: ["exec", "web"]`, and operator `logging.level: "info"`
- `config.patch` exited 1 with `configuration writes are unavailable while --config-layer is active`
- starting with a fourth layer that replaced tenant `allowedOrigins` exited 1 with `ControlledByEarlierLayer`
- the configured canonical config path remained absent, proving the layered lifecycle did not materialize or mutate it
- complete successful run: 38.3 seconds

target.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child
target.body:
Fixes #106778

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a dashboard child from an active Codex-backed channel session (Control UI → new dashboard chat — an ordinary child creation, not a fork) succeeds but **retires the parent session's Codex binding**, even though the parent remains the channel's current session. The next inbound parent turn then fails permanently with `Codex binding generation was retired`, recoverable only by manual SQLite surgery.

Root-cause chain (all on current `main`):
1. `createGatewaySession` emits a terminal `session_end(reason:"new")` on the **parent** for any parent-linked child when `emitCommandHooks === true` — `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`.
2. The Codex extension treats `"new"` as terminal (`ENDED_SESSION_REASONS`) and its `session_end` handler calls `bindingStore.retireSessionGeneration()` — `extensions/codex/index.ts:48,274`.
3. The next lease attempt observes the retired generation and throws `Codex binding generation was retired`.

A detached dashboard child (its own `agent:<id>:dashboard:*` key) runs **in parallel** — it does not replace the parent as the channel's current session, so emitting a terminal `session_end` on the parent is wrong.

## Approach

The parent/child rollover pairs a terminal `session_end(parent)` with a `session_start(child)` — but that pairing is only correct when the child actually **succeeds** the parent. A detached dashboard child and a fork run in *parallel*: the parent stays current. So the two events are split — only the parent `session_end` is gated; the child's `session_start` always fires, because the child was in fact created:

```ts
const childSucceedsParent =
  params.fork !== true &&
  parseAgentSessionKey(target.canonicalKey)?.rest.startsWith("dashboard:") !== true;

if (canonicalParentSessionKey && parentSessionTarget && params.emitCommandHooks === true) {
  if (childSucceedsParent) {
    emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook({ /* parent, reason:"new" */ });
  }
  emitGatewaySessionStartPluginHook({ /* child */ });
}
```

- **Detached dashboard child** / **fork** → no terminal `session_end` on the parent (the #106778 fix; also stops an accepted fork from retiring the parent binding), but the child still receives its `session_start`.
- **Legitimate rollover unchanged**: explicit `/new` successors use non-dashboard keys (`tui-*`) and still emit both; main reset-in-place emits its own hooks via `performGatewaySessionReset` and returns earlier.
- The parent's `before_reset` / `command:new` hooks (documented Control UI behavior, #76957) are untouched.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stale unanswered calls could trigger repeated provider hangup attempts every 30 seconds when an earlier hangup was still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stale-call reaper now keeps one hangup attempt per call ID in flight and releases that guard only after the attempt settles. Existing stale-call predicates, interval cadence, failure logging, and later retries remain unchanged.

## User Impact

### 2026-07-14 exact-head controlled stale-call lifecycle proof

- Scope: the committed regression test invokes the production `startStaleCallReaper()` loop with the real stale-call predicates and cleanup chain. It replaces only the provider-owned `CallManager.endCall()` boundary with a deferred structured result and advances the production 30-second interval with fake timers.

## What Problem This Solves

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw cron run` (a manual/operator run) on a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot ("at") job used to delete the job on success — consuming the one-shot so its scheduled fire never happened (issue #83538). Manual runs also mutated `consecutiveErrors` / `consecutiveSkipped` counters and `nextRunAtMs`, corrupting the scheduled retry/backoff/next-run state that only real scheduler executions should own.

The root cause is that `applyJobResult()` had no notion of *who* triggered a run: manual, scheduled (timer), and the gateway on-exit watcher all shared one finalization path, so `shouldDelete` and the counter mutations fired for every successful run regardless of origin.

## Why This Change Was Made

Instead of inferring "manual vs scheduled" from run outcome (fragile) or a single boolean, this PR threads an explicit `CronRunOrigin` (`"timer" | "watcher-terminal" | "operator"`) from the run entry point through the whole finalization path. Origin is the accurate ownership model:

- `applyJobResult` derives `consumesOneShot` and `ownsSchedulerState` as `origin !== "operator"`, and records `lastRunWasManual = origin === "operator"`.
- Operator runs record the outcome only — they never consume a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot and never touch scheduler counters / `nextRunAtMs` / enabled state.
- `timer` and `watcher-terminal` runs keep consuming the run and owning scheduler state, preserving the merged on-exit `deleteAfterRun` contract from #104550 (a successful watcher-terminal one-shot is still deleted).

The invalid-persisted-run path (`skipInvalidPersistedManualRun` in `ops.ts`) previously hard-coded `origin: "operator"`. Because the gateway on-exit watcher reaches that path with `origin: "watcher-terminal"`, an invalid persisted watcher run was mis-attributed as operator, diverging scheduler-owned counters/alerts/terminal state from other watcher executions. The caller origin is now forwarded through preflight into that finalization so every path carries the true origin.

## User Impact

- Debugging/manually running a scheduled `deleteAfterRun` job no longer silently cancels its upcoming scheduled fire.
- Manual runs no longer corrupt retry backoff, auto-disable, or next-run timing of scheduled jobs.
- Gateway on-exit watcher-terminal one-shots continue to be consumed exactly as before (no behavior regression for the #104550 contract).
- Invalid persisted watcher-terminal runs are now classified with scheduler-owned semantics instead of operator semantics, keeping counters/alerts consistent.

## Evidence

Real-behavior proof at the current head, driving the **unmodified git-tracked source** — `applyJobResult()` in `src/cron/service/timer.ts` and the store mutation in `applyOutcomeToStoredJob()` — through all three origins on a `deleteAfterRun` one-shot. Run inside a `node:24-bookworm-slim` container (container node v24.18.0, the supported runtime floor is 24.15.0) with the repo's own vitest, and corroborated by the committed regression suite.

```
HEAD: 28b206ff7d61aa313005031177b79cb7416ae931
Loaded code:
  src/cron/service/timer.ts :: applyJobResult()
    consumesOneShot    = origin !== "operator"
    ownsSchedulerState = origin !== "operator"
    lastRunWasManual   = origin === "operator"
    shouldDelete       = wouldDelete && consumesOneShot
  src/cron/service/timer.ts :: applyOutcomeToStoredJob()
    if (shouldDelete) store.jobs = jobs.filter(e => e.id !== job.id)
  src/cron/service/ops.ts   :: skipInvalidPersistedManualRun()
    applyJobResult(..., { origin: params.origin })   // caller origin forwarded

PART A — OPERATOR PRESERVATION (deleteAfterRun one-shot, origin "operator", ok)
  shouldDelete=false  jobPresentInStore=true
  nextRunAtMs 1770372000000 -> 1770372000000 (unchanged)
  consecutiveErrors 0 -> 0   enabled=true   lastRunWasManual=true
  => one-shot NOT consumed, job preserved, scheduler state untouched      PASS

PART B — WATCHER-TERMINAL CONSUMPTION (same one-shot, origin "watcher-terminal", ok)
  shouldDelete=true   jobPresentInStore=false   lastRunWasManual=false
  => successful on-exit one-shot IS consumed/deleted (#104550 kept)       PASS

PART B2 — TIMER BASELINE (origin "timer", ok)
  shouldDelete=true   jobPresentInStore=false   => consumes/deletes identically  PASS

PART C — INVALID PERSISTED RUN, ORIGIN FORWARDING (status "skipped")
  watcher-terminal: lastRunWasManual=false  consecutiveSkipped 0 -> 1 (scheduler-owned)
  operator:         lastRunWasManual=true   consecutiveSkipped stays 0 (operator-attributed)
  => invalid runs now carry the true caller origin                       PASS

Harness result (container node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.9): 4 passed (4)
Committed regression suite src/cron/service/ops.regression.test.ts: 21 passed (21)
OVERALL: PASS
```

The regression suite adds parametrized coverage asserting watcher-terminal invalid runs keep scheduled/consuming scheduler-state semantics while operator invalid runs stay operator-attributed.

Closes #106943

## Summary

**Problem:** 用户设置格式错误的 ElevenLabs `baseUrl` 时，会在调用链深处收到 `new URL()` 抛出的原始 `TypeError: Invalid URL`，无法确定是 ElevenLabs baseUrl 配置的问题。

**Solution:** 在 `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` 中添加 URL 格式校验，遵循 #105334 的 Deepgram 模式：解析 URL、校验 scheme 是否合法（仅 http/https）、对非法输入抛出描述性错误。为 realtime provider 增加独立的 `normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl`，额外接受 `ws`/`wss` scheme，保持 WebSocket 端点兼容。URL builder 将 `http→ws`、`https→wss` 转换，同时保留直接 `ws`/`wss` 地址不变。

**What changed / NOT changed:** 修改了 `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts`（normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl 增加 URL 校验）和 `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts`（新增 realtime 独立校验函数 + WS URL 构造）。未变更：REST callers（speech、TTS、media understanding）的调用方式不变；已有配置项无需迁移；默认值（空/undefined）行为不变；不涉及性能优化。

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users setting a malformed ElevenLabs `baseUrl` would receive a raw `TypeError: Invalid URL` from `new URL()` deeper in the call chain, with no indication the misconfiguration was in the ElevenLabs baseUrl setting.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: ElevenLabs baseUrl validation — REST normalizer (`normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl`) validates HTTP/HTTPS only with descriptive errors; Realtime normalizer (`normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl`) validates HTTP/HTTPS/WS/WSS; WebSocket URL builder (`toElevenLabsRealtimeWsUrl`) preserves all accepted schemes.

**Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw development worktree (`fix/issue-106943-elevenlabs-baseurl-validate`), Node.js v24.18.0, tsx runner, branch HEAD `8c0da723a5`. Real ElevenLabs production API accessed via `xi-api-key` (redacted) at `api.elevenlabs.io`. OpenClaw Gateway started on port 18999 with `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: (1) `node .../behavior-proof.mjs` — 22/22 module scenarios (2) `curl https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices` — real API HTTP 200 (3) live module validation with before/after comparison (4) `curl http://127.0.0.1:18999/healthz` — Gateway `{"ok":true}`

**After-fix evidence**: Before: `TypeError: Invalid URL` (raw). After: `Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL` (clear). Real API `api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices` → HTTP 200. Gateway health → `{"ok":true}`. Exact-head (`8c0da723a5`) module test — 22/22 pass. Terminal transcript:
```
═══ BEFORE FIX (simulating old behavior) ═══
  normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl("not-a-url")
  → TypeError: Invalid URL (raw, buried deep in call chain)

═══ AFTER FIX (exact head 8c0da723a5 — 22/22 pass) ═══
  normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl("not-a-url")
  → "Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL" (clear, actionable!)
  normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl("ftp://files.example.com")
  → "Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: unsupported scheme "ftp:" (expected http or https)"
  normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl("wss://api.elevenlabs.io")
  → "Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: unsupported scheme "wss:" (expected http or https)"

═══ Module functions tested on exact head 8c0da723a5 ═══
  REST (11):  default→https://api.elevenlabs.io, valid HTTPS→preserved,
    custom path→preserved, query params→preserved, trailing slash→stripped,
    malformed→"Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL",
    FTP→"unsupported scheme", WSS→"unsupported scheme"
  Realtime (7): default, HTTPS, HTTP, WSS, WS, malformed→error, FTP→error
  WS URL (4): HTTPS→wss://, HTTP→ws://, direct WSS/WS preserved

═══ Real ElevenLabs API (production) ═══
  GET https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/voices → HTTP 200 ✅
  GET https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/models → HTTP 200 ✅ (14 models)

═══ OpenClaw Gateway (port 18999) ═══
```

commands.review_summary:
The PR adds a single-flight interval guard and a 15-second Discord REST timeout to thread-binding sweeps, with regression coverage for overlap and recovery paths.

PR surface: Source +60, Tests +362. Total +422 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level with high confidence: current main starts each interval tick independently while `runSweepOnce` can remain blocked on an awaited Discord REST probe. The supplied baseline and controlled-runtime transcripts demonstrate the resulting request multiplication, although this review did not execute a new reproduction locally.
